parts.gloss: those who do not know or practice

words.gloss: those who do not know or practice

literal: Those who do not know other things except theft, having done things beyond measure, will perish right there.
translation: Those who know nothing other than deceitful theft will commit boundless wrongs and perish at that very moment.
modern: திருட்டைத் தவிர வேறு நல்வழிகளை அறியாதவர்கள், நெறிமுறையற்ற செயல்களைச் செய்து அந்த கணத்திலேயே அழிந்து போவார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet warns about the ultimate fate of habitual thieves. Those who do not know or practice any honest means of livelihood other than stealing ('kaḷavu alla maṟṟaiya tēṟṟātavar') will inevitably commit boundless, unlawful acts ('aḷavalla ceytu'). Because they lack moral boundaries, their actions lead to their immediate ruin ('āṅkē vīvar'). The word 'aḷavu' here refers to the limits of righteousness and law, which thieves constantly transgress.
